title: MGLRU flushes a page-generation batch into a dying child after memcg reparenting

classification.cwe_mapping_note: These are evaluator classifications; the linked Linux CVE announcement does not assign an official CWE.

finding.stale_target: The page-table walker batches a generation move without the lruvec lock, then later flushes it through the cached child lruvec even though memcg offlining has reparented that child in the meantime.
finding.control_flow: A one-page child starts in generation 0, the walker changes the page to generation 1 and batches [-1,+1], reparenting moves the unadjusted [1,0] counters to the parent, and the delayed flush writes [-1,+1] back into the dying child.
finding.impact: The dying child retains nonzero generation counters while the parent reports zero pages in the generation that actually contains the page. This violates the memcg-exit invariant and models the premature-OOM impact described for CVE-2026-80719.
finding.security_property: A delayed MGLRU generation batch must be committed to the first live lruvec that owns the reparented pages; no accounting delta may be committed to a dying child after its counters have moved.
finding.expected_fix: At flush time, check whether the cached lruvec belongs to a dying memcg and redirect the batch to its first non-dying ancestor before locking and updating generation counters.
finding.model_boundary: The request uses one bounded 4 KiB MiniMM note and transient signed counters for two generations. It never creates a host cgroup, enables host MGLRU, walks host page tables, induces memory pressure, triggers OOM, or executes a real data race or assertion.
